column1: What is the exact mathematical identity underlying autoregressive LLM training (chain rule factorization)?
column2: P(x) = Π_{t=1}^{T} P(x_t | x_1,...,x_{t-1}) — the joint probability of a sequence factors exactly into the product of conditional next-token probabilities, with no approximation involved.

column1: Why can't bidirectional (masked, BERT-style) models generate text natively like autoregressive models?
column2: Bidirectional models learn P(x_t | x_{≠t}), conditioning on both past and future context, but generation requires sampling left-to-right from P(x_t | x_{<t}). They need heuristics like iterative refinement or masked diffusion to generate at all.

column1: Why must positional information be explicitly injected into a transformer's input?
column2: Because self-attention is permutation-equivariant — it computes weighted sums agnostic to token order — so without explicit positional encoding the model cannot distinguish token order.

column1: What is the key mathematical property of sinusoidal positional encodings that enables relative position learning?
column2: For any fixed offset k, PE_{pos+k} can be expressed as a linear function of PE_pos, allowing the model to learn to attend based on relative position.

column1: What is the critical advantage of Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) over additive sinusoidal encoding?
column2: RoPE rotates query/key vector pairs by an angle proportional to position, so the dot product between two positionally-encoded vectors depends only on their relative distance, not absolute positions — making it a relative encoding baked directly into attention.

column1: What is the dominant bottleneck in LLM inference, and why?
column2: Memory bandwidth, not compute throughput. Single-token decode has very low arithmetic intensity (~1 FLOP/byte vs. an H100 ridge point of ~295 FLOPs/byte), so GPU compute units sit idle waiting on HBM reads of weights and KV-cache.

column1: What is the 'ridge point' in the roofline model, and what does it mean for a workload to be below it?
column2: The ridge point is the arithmetic intensity (FLOPs/byte) at which a system transitions from memory-bound to compute-bound, calculated as peak FLOPS / peak bandwidth (e.g., ~295 FLOPs/byte on H100). Workloads below this point are memory-bound — performance is limited by data movement, not math throughput.

column1: What is the formula for KV-cache memory size, and what do the factor-of-2 and each variable represent?
column2: KV_cache_bytes = 2 × L × H × d_head × S × bytes_per_element. The 2 accounts for storing both keys and values; L = layers, H = KV attention heads, d_head = head dimension, S = sequence length.

column1: How does increasing batch size affect arithmetic intensity during LLM decode, and why does this matter?
column2: Arithmetic intensity scales roughly proportionally with batch size (more FLOPs per byte of weights loaded, since weights are reused across the batch), which can shift decode from memory-bound toward compute-bound, improving GPU utilization.

column1: Why does Grouped Query Attention (GQA) reduce KV-cache size compared to standard multi-head attention?
column2: GQA uses fewer key/value heads (H) than query heads, sharing K/V projections across groups of query heads. Since KV-cache size scales linearly with H, this directly shrinks cache memory requirements (e.g., LLaMA-3 70B uses only 8 KV heads via GQA).

column1: What is prefix caching (prompt/KV caching), and what phase of inference does it optimize?
column2: Prefix caching stores the computed Key/Value tensors for a prompt prefix so that requests sharing that prefix can skip recomputation of it. It optimizes the prefill phase (compute-bound, O(n²·d)) by allowing decode to begin immediately on the shared portion.

column1: What distinguishes the prefill phase from the decode phase in autoregressive transformer inference?
column2: Prefill processes the entire prompt in one parallel forward pass (compute-bound, O(n²·d) attention cost); decode generates tokens one at a time, reading the full accumulated KV-cache from HBM each step (memory-bandwidth-bound).
